doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Chess reissues and Moody's Flute 'N The Blues
summary: He edited Chess reissues in the sixties and produced James Moody's Flute 'N The Blues.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Woody Herman and Nat Cole - and he’s a jazz instigator like I am, he’s from Chicago, he’s passed now - he got me on at Chess and I started doing re-issues for them. I’d go through the vaults with Phil Chess and he’d say, “Oh, this box is so-and-so and that box is so-and-so.” No writing on there, he just knew, and I’d take them out and I’d edit them, and I did the first James Moody album, Flute ‘N The Blues.
That’s where I met Johnny Coles, and Clarence Johnston, his drummer, Jimmy Boyd his pianist and F horn player, and Tom McIntosh, and Eddy Jefferson. They were all in that band.
